descriptionChirho: To surround, close in on, or encircle a person or place in a hostile or threatening manner, often describing enemies or dangers closing in.
To go around, encircle, or make a circuit around something in a non-hostile sense, such as a processional march around a city or descriptive encircling of a location.
To round off or cut in a circle, specifically referring to the cultic prohibition against rounding the corners of the head (trimming hair in a circular fashion).
To complete a round or cycle of recurring events, describing days or periods that have come full circle.
